historical_references.reference: Chhaya was an ancient Indian courtesan mentioned in the Sanskrit epic Mahabharata. She was renowned for her beauty and grace, and was often compared to a shadow (Chhaya in Sanskrit means shadow). She played an instrumental role in the Mahabharata war, using her charms to help Arjuna win over Draupadi during the game of dice.

Chhaya Devi was a 16th century Rajput queen of Mewar, Rajasthan. She was the wife of Rana Sangram Singh II, and played a significant role in the defense of Chittorgarh Fort during the siege by the Mughal Emperor Akbar. She famously immolated herself on the funeral pyre of her husband to uphold the Rajput tradition of Jauhar.
